## 2026-11-16 19:05 - Vendor stock restored; the recovery trigger was the RESET counter, and NetworkManager was stripping the host address

The box is back on the vendor image: OpenWrt 22.03.6 revision 2.4.15, stock kernel
`5.10.201 #0 SMP Sat Nov 25 18:18:57 2023`, 40 `hi_` modules, 2 wiphys
(`/sys/class/ieee80211/phy0`, `phy1`), the wireless calibration loaded on both bands
(`hwifi_rf_cali_file_load_2g succ`, `..._5g succ`, and the cali result written to the device on
both), `192.168.10.1` answering 2/2 pings, and SSH working on the project key.

The flash itself: `hi_upgrade 0x832808a4 0x1380279`, `upgrade soft version: 22.03.06`,
`Flashing kernel...` with the kernel slot erase at `0x0083ffff`, `Flashing rootfs...` writing
15,728,640 bytes with erases at `0x0173ffff` and `0x015fffff` - both kernel slots and both rootfs
partitions. Console: `build/uart-logs/20261116T115756Z-recover-stock.log`.

Two host-side faults cost attempts and are worth recording:

1. **The recovery trigger is the RESET button counter, not a plain hold.** The loader prints
   `RESET button is pressed for: 0 second(s)`, `1 second(s)`, `2 second(s)`, `Resetting...`, and only
   then does the countdown end in `recovery button press` followed by `Using pie@0x10a70000 device`,
   `TFTP from server 192.168.1.88; our IP address is 192.168.1.1`, `Filename 'recovery.bin'.`,
   `Load address: 0x83200000`. The counter only appears on a true power-on reset, never on the
   watchdog resets the box does itself. Evidence:
   `build/uart-logs/20261116T052326Z-recovery-boot.log` and `...2055749Z-plt-recovery.log`.
2. **NetworkManager strips the bench port's IPv4 addresses.** `enp195s0f3u1` sits in
   `connecting (getting IP configuration)`, retries DHCP against a board that is not serving it, and
   removes any address added by hand minutes later. With no address, the board's ARP for
   `192.168.1.88` is unanswered and the console shows `ARP Retry count exceeded; starting again`.
   The fix that held: `nmcli device set enp195s0f3u1 managed no`, then `ip addr add`. The port is
   still unmanaged now.

Correction to the earlier reading: I twice called an `RRQ` in the server log the board's request when
it was my own loopback self-test (`RRQ give up at block 1` is that test reading one block and
leaving). Only `RRQ ...` followed by `RRQ sent 20975775 bytes` from the board proves a transfer.

SSH after the flash needs the project key installed again (the recovered overlay is empty) and
dropbear started with `-R` after deleting the zero-byte host keys.

## 2026-11-17 08:45 - ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED: the 3dh kernel died in luofu_early's ioremap; 3dn boots to userspace, then wedges in a new userspace-stage problem

Diagnostic fire 3dm (3dl kernel + explicit earlycon in the built-in cmdline) gave the first readable
early boot. U-Boot read our uImage (Data Size 2964952), earlycon came up at 0x1010f000, and the
kernel panicked at 0.0 s:

    Unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference at virtual address 00000010
    PC is at kmem_cache_alloc_trace+0xb4/0xd8     r5 = 0x00000000
    ioremap <- luofu_early+0x34 <- setup_arch <- start_kernel

Root cause: luofu_early() (the mach .init_early hook, called from setup_arch before mm_init) called
ioremap(). With the 3dh-era .config (CONFIG_SLAB=y + CONFIG_TRACING=y) kmalloc() compiles to
kmem_cache_alloc_trace(kmalloc_caches[..]) and the kmalloc caches do not exist yet, so the cache
pointer is NULL and the vm-area allocation NULL-derefs. The 3df/3dg builds had no CONFIG_TRACING,
which is why they booted; this is the exact 3dh regression, not a slot/delivery problem.

The panic rebooted (panic=5) into the stock fallback, which now booted healthy and stayed up.
Recovery detour: the guarded S99 hook from the first fire was renamed S99omo-recover.disabled but
procd matches S[0-9][0-9]*, so it kept restoring kernelb and rebooting (~6 cycles, each doing an mtd
write of the stock image). Moved it out of rc.d via the broker lane; kernelb md5 verified back to
stock 0ca1fde627aae581ef4e86441e968363; SSH restored by starting dropbear through the broker.

Fix: move the sysctrl crumb + bootreg flip out of luofu_early() into luofu_early_crumb()
(early_initcall, after mm_init, still before userspace). luofu_early() now only calls
luofu_uart_early(). Patched both the live tree and tools/lab-src (check-lab-src PASS) and built
3dn = 3dl config + earlycon + fix: luofu-slice-phase3dn.bin 3,005,332 B md5
984b0ac9f14a862e658b947665ff9a32, zImage 0e786a1da703d4c225a4e4aaec9ef26e, init 6464a08d (3dk
console-logging), DTB 336ba39e, trailer verified.

U-Boot Data Size 2964536, earlycon, luofu-fmc probe (FMC read path green in the same boot), 18
luofu partitions, Run /init at 14.45 s, the seven /vendor/upper ... OK lines, and procd at 19.54 s.
This is the first boot of the 3dh-era kernel class and it validates the fix.

New problem, same boot: after procd init (~19.5 s) there are no further userspace messages, and at
108 s/171 s the kernel reports rcu_sched stalls ("rcu_sched kthread starved ... cpu=0", 8407/14712

## 2026-11-17 20:40 - RE verdict: hyfi_bridging crash is a vendor sk_buff ABI mismatch, not the bridge hooks; v17 drops hyfi preload and fixes the hook variable ABI

Subagent RE (disassembly of hyfi-bridging.ko/khslink etc.):
- hyfi_netlink_receive (input callback of a vendor-private netlink protocol, id 30/26) does
  skb_clone(); r6 = [clone+0x118]; then stores into [r6+0x40]. That offset is vendor
  skb->data (0x118); in our kernel struct sk_buff is 0xb0 with data at 0xa0. So it reads out of
  bounds and faults. Measured vendor delta: len 0xc8 vs 0x54, data_len 0xcc vs 0x58, headers
  0x106/0x108/0x10a vs 0x8e/0x90/0x92, tail/end/head 0x10c/0x110/0x114 vs 0x94/0x98/0x9c,
  data 0x118 vs 0xa0 = +0x74 for len/data_len and +0x78 from headers on (4-byte vendor field
  between data_len and the bitfields). Anchors: hi_hslink_tx_urarp (skb_reserve), hyfi_bridge_get_dst
  (EtherType from head+mac_header), mc_find_acl_rule (len-data_len).
- The four br_* symbols are exported *pointer variables* in the vendor bridge, not functions:
  hyfi only stores callbacks into them (bridge_get_dst / port_dev_get / br_notify / mc_process).
  Our previous function stubs were ABI-wrong (a store would overwrite the stub's first
  instruction). Also the vendor bridge patches that would consume those pointers are not in our
  tree, so "real" hook semantics cannot be reconstructed offline.
- net_device side now matches (WEXT layout: priv_flags 0x13c, netdev_ops 0x128, sizeof 0x540);
  the remaining hyfi needs (net_bridge cache at netdev_priv+0x10, vendor skb private bytes) come
  from vendor-only bridge patches, i.e. a full vendor-bridge port, not a quick fix.

v17 (this build): remove hyfi-bridging from the preload list (it must not run on the vendor sk_buff
ABI), and replace the four exported function stubs with writable zeroed exported pointer variables.
No sk_buff ABI change. Slice 2,906,100 B md5 8342ccb9c0167766529277719330f43c (zImage a08ffc66,
init 74033a38). This is the "known-good stack without hyfi" test; the vendor userspace tolerated
hyfi's absence in the 2026-11-14 stack.

## 2026-11-18 09:15 - TEXT_OFFSET early-boot fix (patch 003): full 6.18 kernel compile RC=0 with the real, non-encodable offset; load address verified 0x80608000

Problem: textofs-$(CONFIG_ARCH_LUOFU) := 0x00608000 is required by the stock-loader address
derivation (stage 0x83200000 -> (stage & 0xf8000000) + TEXT_OFFSET = 0x80608000) but 0x00608000 is
not an encodable ARM rotated immediate, so stock 6.18 fails in arch/arm/kernel/head.S:123/:188
(pgtbl macro) and arch/arm/boot/compressed/head.S:312/:410 with "invalid constant (608000)".

Fix (opensource/target-skeleton/target/linux/hisilicon/patches-6.18/003-arm-textofs-nonimmediate.patch,
sha256 407352b8aced76da6c6f1fcef53c77bca0221473515c144126cbe3358e707f5c): use the kernel's own
mov_l macro to materialize TEXT_OFFSET instead of an immediate add/sub at the four sites:
- arch/arm/kernel/head.S: pgtbl macro -> mov_l rd, TEXT_OFFSET; add rd, rd, @phys; and the
  PHYS_OFFSET recovery -> mov_l r5, TEXT_OFFSET; sub r8, r8, r5.
- arch/arm/boot/compressed/head.S: final kernel image address -> mov_l r4, TEXT_OFFSET; add
  r4, r0, r4; and the zreladdr-relative adjustment -> mov_l r0, TEXT_OFFSET; sub r0, r4, r0.
mov_l expands to movw/movt on the target (CONFIG_CPU_V7) and to an ldr literal-pool load for older
CPUs; pristine-6.18.60 dry-run passes; no make override or WERROR workaround is used.

Verified in ~/openwrt-lab (openwrt main 27663a0, linux-6.18.60, tree's
OpenWrt GCC 14.4.0 toolchain): make target/linux/prepare RC=0 (patches 001/002/003 apply, no
.rej), make target/linux/compile -j16 RC=0; invalid-constant errors 0; arch/arm/boot/zImage
produced (sha256 45ad00d502ed7b2386f83db794e9015267f4f9d66de8d0deaab8aca24cf18d10).
Address story verified from the built artifacts: head objects compiled with
-DTEXT_OFFSET=0x00608000 (no override); vmlinux _text = 0xc0608000 with PAGE_OFFSET=0xc0000000;
linked stext recovers PHYS_OFFSET via adr_l _text + movw/movt 0x608000 (disasm
05-disasm-kernel-head.txt); physical _text = 0x80608000 == computed load address; uImage
mkdir must use -a/-e 0x80608000. An incremental rebuild (03b-rebuild) also RC=0.
Local-only evidence: build/linux-kbuild/waves/upstream-6.18-textoffset-20261118/ (00-README index,
baseline/fix logs and rc files, zImage sha, link/load derivation, kernel-head and compressed-head
disassemblies, pre-ARMv7 literal-pool fallback check, patch sha/dry-run). Gitignored; not
published; the zImage is an intermediate compile product, not a deliverable image.

Docs updated: target-skeleton README + opensource/docs/SKELETON-SMOKE.md (dated section: defect,
approach, exact commands, address proof, what it does/does not prove, updated blockers); root
STATUS/EVIDENCE-INDEX/README record that the kernel now compiles with the correct offset and the

  drivers/watchdog/luofu-wdt.c, .../watchdog/hisilicon,luofu-wdt.yaml, watchdog

  .set_timeout), CONFIG_LUOFU_WDT=y.
- config-6.18 +18 lines: LUOFU_CRG/LUOFU_WDT =y plus MFD_SYSCON/REGMAP/REGMAP_MMIO selects
  with [N] provenance markers; canonical re-derivation symbol-identical (286 symbols,
  KCONFIG_UNCHANGED). DTS rewritten to the bindings: CRG node is
  "hisilicon,luofu-crg","syscon","simple-mfd" with #clock-cells=1/#reset-cells=2 and only the
  watchdog child; no gate children, no vendor props, no duplicate unit address.

Design decisions:
- Shared 0x14880000 page: one syscon+simple-mfd node, one regmap; CRG driver and watchdog child
  both call syscon_node_to_regmap(), so neither maps or request_mem_region()s the page (0 call
  sites verified). This removes the lab bug where CRG claimed the page and the watchdog probe
  returned -EBUSY. Rejected: two nodes with overlapping reg + bare ioremap.
- Clock gates are a driver-side table indexed by dt-binding IDs (0..15 kept as ABI), not 16 fake
  child nodes without reg. Includes a missing-entry probe check.
- Reset cells kept 2-cell (CRG offset, bit), range-checked to 0x2c/0x30/0x34 so a specifier
  cannot write watchdog/softrst/mux/PLL words; rcdev.of_reset_n_cells=2 fixes the lab
  devm_reset_control_array_get() -EINVAL root cause.
- Watchdog: vendor value pairs/order preserved exactly (enable val1->val0 @0x64, stop val0->val1,
  ping reset0->reset1 @0x70, hwver-2 (secs-1) bits[18:10] @0x50 mask 0xfff803ff); probe performs
  zero register accesses; no restart handler (vendor sysctrl/bootreg reset path not understood -
  documented TODO; no IRQ claimed).

  select MFD_SYSCON), bindings for the reboot node and a new hisilicon,luofu-sysctrl syscon node.

  never invents the stock value); (2) write the vendor softrst_val0/1 pair 0x51162100/0xaee9deff
  to the CRG reboot word at page offset 0x00; (3) if that does not take, arm the CRG watchdog

  shared syscon regmaps; probe performs no register access; writes confined to selector/reboot/
  watchdog words (never soft-reset 0x84, mux, PLL).

  correctly; no consumer code change needed.

## 2026-11-18 16:55 - 0x21 selector semantics integrated, patch 017 corrected, boot-time pair recorder added, final image rebuilt (362ca4ec) and install harness 100/100

0x21 research (opensource/docs/SELECTOR-0x21.md, 926 lines incl. resolution section; 129 [V]/20 [U]/
6 [X]): reconstructed from read-only U-Boot disassembly, env dumps and bench records:
- The selector is the 32-bit SYSCTRL cell 0x10100C08; the env blocks (enva mtd3/envb mtd4, one
  128 KiB block each crc32-le(4)|flags(1)|data(131067)) hold bootcmd=bootflag pair selection.
- The env bootflag is the ACTUAL pair selector; the cell is the failure record. The loader prints
  bootflag/bootreg, initialises the cell from env when 0 (10/11), and bootfip stores the OPPOSITE
  pair's low byte before Linux starts (0x11 for an A boot, 0x10 for B). A recorded value that
  contradicts env means "last boot of that pair failed": loader re-stamps env to the other pair
  and boots it. A successful boot therefore requires userspace to re-record the running pair
  (vendor hsd_appm boot_done, ~16-30 s).
- 0x21 is the PROJECT'S bench value (FLASH-PLAN/fire-device), not vendor-written; the vendor
  userspace writes only 0x10/0x11. 0x21 boots B when env=b, bootfip then stores 0x10, and 0x21
  never persists; a true POR clears the cell to 0 (43/43 POR sequences). A 0x21/bad handover
  cannot strand the box (RESET-hold/TFTP recovery is entered after a POR that clears the cell).
- Driver/installer implications: patch 017's claim that the vendor writes 0x21 was unsupported;
  the store must be a low-byte RMW preserving the upper 24 bits (upper meaning [U]); and our
  target was missing the boot-time pair-recorder service, so the installer's two-witness check
  would refuse on our own system and the first reboot after a normal boot could silently flip
  pairs.

Selector fixes (patch 017, sha c991aaa50419f4b6ba0c9a37018a682c0a7a5afc66d43c611c947af25cce0f1d):
- corrected comments/ABI/Kconfig/YAML: 0x21 = project bench value, env selects and cell records
  failure, vendor writes only 0x10/0x11; store is now a low-byte RMW preserving upper 24 bits with
  whole-cell read-back; probe remains register-free.
- new target image service base-files/etc/init.d/luofu_record_pair (START=96, enabled as
  S96luofu_record_pair): determines the booted rootfs slot from UBI mtd_num + /proc/mtd label
  (optional ubi.mtd= cross-check), bounded wait for the selector sysfs, maps to pair a/b, writes
  the running pair, logs, idempotent, fail-safe (never manual-b/uninitialised/unknown, never
  touches env/mtd/devmem).
- platform.sh comments corrected (env is the selector; handover via the loader mismatch path;
  two-witness valid because of the recorder; non-fatal warning if the recorder is absent;
  refusals unchanged). Harness extended with recorder scenarios: 94/94 fixture assertions and
  100/100 with the real rebuilt container.

Upstream review-form series regenerated consistently: commit message 0017 rewritten, series/0017
and 01-commit-messages regenerated via gen-series.py --check, validation logs/hashes replaced,

Patch 019-arm-clk-luofu-clock-tree.patch (sha256
9d86498b405e43cc05b77b46b5ce74d4dfa5256a3dd6f444690d85e0cbc0513c):
- drivers/clk/hisilicon/crg-luofu.c: all 16 gates parented on the real decoded parents (apb, ahb,
  gemacN, lsw_dp, lsw_pfe) via DT clocks/clock-names and of_clk_get_parent_name; two READ-ONLY PLL
  providers (0x198/0x1e0; status word 0x90 bits 30/27, busy bit 7) implementing recalc_rate/
  is_enabled only - no set_rate, because the vendor writer/relock protocol's feedback-word encoding
  is inconsistent with the recalc path and a wrong store can hang the core; two READ-ONLY muxes
  (0x138 bit 3 CPU / bit 1 efuse) with get_parent only (set_parent = -EOPNOTSUPP; CPU mux never
  writable); CLK_IGNORE_UNUSED on gates; probe remains register-free; provisional-0x20 wording
  retired.
- dt-bindings header: IDs 16-19 appended (PLL_CPU/PLL_LSW/CPU_MUX/EFUSE_MUX, NR=20); existing 16
  IDs not renumbered. YAML: required 7-input clocks/clock-names + read-only PLL/mux description.
  No new config symbols (CONFIG_LUOFU_CRG unchanged).
- Shared DTS: four missing fixed clocks (gemacN_clk 125 MHz, lsw_dp_clk 166 MHz, lsw_pfe_clk
  333 MHz, efuse_ring_clk 20 MHz) + CRG clock tree; TARGET-DESIGN 6.2/7.1, README, SKELETON-SMOKE
  section and MISC-SOC-BLOCKS 5.3 correction (bit-3 polarity + decoded equation).

Decode evidence: vendor hi_clk.ko (GPL, unstripped, 15,556 B, md5 3b331b9058e13bc409dd8f0040af3b11,
identical in both rootfs): hi_pll_recalc_rate = parent * (int + frac/2^24) / fbdiv, then non-zero
divider-select fields word0[10:8]/word0[6:4] each add a div-factor (absent here = 0); bit 3 of word0
byte 0 = integer-only mode; word0 byte3[5:0] = feedback divider; bit 7 = writer busy.

Patch 020 (sha256 806a113c9dc581ccb3d9248f1298f4cf8a48e1645228b525b1a4853f70bfa6e8, 2,148
lines, 6 files) rewrites luofu-pie.c from the patch-015 scaffold into a ring engine and extends
luofu-gmac.c into a phylink/netdev front end:
- coherent 32-byte descriptor rings for the measured 2 RX / 2 TX channels (log2 8 RX descriptors
  + 1536 B buffers, log2 12 TX descriptors); recovered v250 global/per-channel init sequence;
  mask-all -> unmask-active; global RX enable via 0x3200 bit0; four IRQs with the recovered
  schedule/mask/ack order; NAPI RX poll that recycles completions but deliberately does NOT decode
  the [U] status/length words; TX producer with poll-only completion; read-back verification tears
  the engine down on mismatch.
- Fail-closed arm gate: probe validates resources/ring tables and refuses with -EOPNOTSUPP before
  any register write, clock enable, reset toggle or IRQ unless luofu_pie.arm=1 on the cmdline; DTS
  stays disabled. GEMAC only registers a netdev once the backend is armed, forwards
  ndo_start_xmit to PIE, and writes only the measured 1 Gbps MAC link-up/down words (other speeds
  warn instead of guessing). New luofu-pie.h + GPL-exported backend; binding gains required
  rx-ring/tx-ring tables; Kconfig GMAC->PIE dependency and select PHYLINK (CONFIG_PHYLINK m->y is
  the only symbol change).

## 2026-11-19 13:45 - MILESTONE: our kernel 6.18.60 + our OpenWrt rootfs BOOTED TO USERSPACE on the WR3000 v2 (attended)

Boot chain (UART evidence, build/evidence-firstboot/uart-boot8-SUCCESS.log + SUCCESS.md):
U-Boot failover "bootflag a bootreg 11 -> boot from kernela failed, change to kernelb" ->
Image Name Linux-6.18.60 -> our kernel banner, 2 CPUs (SMP release) -> UBI attached mtd14
"rootfsb" -> block ubiblock0_0 created from the static squashfs volume -> VFS mounted root
(squashfs, read-only) -> /sbin/init -> init console/watchdog/preinit -> procd early/watchdog/
ubus/init -> kmodloader -> urngd -> overlayfs (tmpfs fallback) -> "Please press Enter to
activate this console." FIRST FULL BOOT OF OUR OWN OS ON THIS HARDWARE.

The five bugs between the first kernel banner and userspace (all fixed in the target tree):
1. Stock U-Boot supplies NO kernel command line for our uImage (first boot: empty cmdline ->
   VFS root panic). A /chosen/bootargs DTB property made U-Boot itself crash (data abort before
   hand-off). Working fix: CONFIG_CMDLINE + CONFIG_CMDLINE_FORCE with the root/ubi args.
2. ubiblock rounds a UBI volume down to 512 B, so the squashfs payload must be padded before
   ubinize. luofu-image.py rootfs-ubi gained --pad-align; the recipe pads to 4096 B.
3. OpenWrt's squashfs is XZ with the ARM BCJ filter ("Filters selected: arm"); the kernel
   lacked CONFIG_XZ_DEC_ARM=y, so every compressed file block failed with "xz decompression
   failed" while the raw FMC reads were byte-perfect (verified with per-page CRC against the
   host image: 900/900 pages matched). Enabling CONFIG_XZ_DEC_ARM=y fixed the decompression.
4. The first-install tool's raw full-partition hash check for the rootfs was invalid because
   ubiformat rewrites UBI EC-header image_seq; replaced with tools/ubi-volume-check.py (parses
   the UBI volume payload on both sides and compares used_ebs/data_pad/payload sha256).
5. The SYSENV boot_reg sysfs write must be a single write; a tty-split printf wrote partial
   values. echo -n "0x11" > boot_reg works and was used for the handover in the no-SSH path.

Install path used: stock -> broker/telnet root shell (box-provision --telnetd) -> wget the
kernel/rootfs from a host HTTP server -> device-side write_pair script (mtd erase/write kernelb,
ubiformat rootfsb, read-backs; semantic UBI verify read-only via ubiattach) -> selector 0x11 ->
warm reboot -> loader failover. The first-install tool's fail-closed logic (partition by label,
inactive pair only, full read-backs, selector last, recovery plan) was followed manually because
the recovered stock has no SSH/dropbear; its SSH UART-detection bug was also fixed for next time.

Artifacts: clean production image rebuilt without the temporary CRC-debug patch:
bin/targets/hisilicon/luofu/openwrt-hisilicon-luofu-cudy_wr3000-v2-squashfs-sysupgrade.bin
6,185,262 B sha256 e893c388e4ab8be61be0f76cd00b003000516005fef3d20bef5b26ecf853c8b5 (config
CMDLINE/XZ verified; NOT re-flashed). The image running on the box is the debug-CRC kernel
(sha256 kernel slot 897d4926...) from image 51baf2ac..., kept running for observation.

Observed remaining gaps: no network (LSW/PIE/GEMAC netdevs not wired yet), no persistent
overlay (image has no rootfs_data volume; tmpfs fallback), /lib/functions/board.sh missing for
board_detect. Box currently runs our image with console only; recovery door was armed and the
stock fallback path is proven.

## 2026-11-20 15:05 - RX path is functionally alive after W16: PIE RX completions arrive, but our decoder drops them (status 0x25, port 0) and host traffic still is not forwarded to the CPU

Image 437a0766 (patches 001-052; heartbeat; full W3-W16 + luofu_pie.rxtrace=1) installed from stock
and booted; W16 static GEMAC config verified (0x1c=1, 0x100=0x33400600); heartbeat continuous.
With the RX completion trace, after the host traffic test the PIE RX channel 0 fired and completed
frames:
  pie-trace RXpoll ch=0 hw_rptr=1..6 sw_rptr=0..6 delta=1
  pie-trace RXCOMP ch=0 idx=0..5 hw_rptr=1..6 ret=-5 len=60 status=37 port=0 vlan=0
    desc=6000003c 824600c2 0100b125 00000380 00000000  (DMA address increments by 0x800 per frame)
So the PIE RX ring and interrupt path DO work after the W16 GEMAC config - first RX activity ever.
But:
- our decoder rejects every completion because status=0x25 (37) is nonzero (the decoder treats any
  nonzero status as an error) and because port=0 has no registered netdev (we expect 8..12);
- the frames are ~60-byte periodic one-per-second control/management frames, not the host's ARP
  requests; host ping still fails and the sniff sees only host ARPs.
Interpretation: RX is functioning for switch-generated/control frames (CPU port 0), while host
ingress frames are still not forwarded to the CPU - likely the L2/VLAN/port-forwarding state
(the CFE-installed runtime tables absent because the vendor modules cannot load on 6.18), or the
RX completion status/port semantics differ from the decoded model (0x25 may include valid tags/class
bits, and port 0 may be the CPU port that should map to a netdev).
Next: QM lane to decode the RX completion status/port fields properly and determine what state is
needed to get host frames forwarded to the CPU (CFE L2/VLAN/port config), then a gated stage or a
targeted test (e.g., unicast probe to the box MAC) to confirm. Evidence 2026-11-20-rxtrace.log.

## 2026-11-20 15:30 - FIRST REAL TRAFFIC: box accepts a punted ARP exception on eth2 and sends an ARP reply on the wire

Image e924f8a6 (patches 001-053; full W3-W16 + luofu_pie.rxdiag=1 accepterr=1; heartbeat) installed
from stock and booted; W16 verified; heartbeat continuous.
Host traffic test (ping 192.168.1.1 from the bench link):
- PIE RX ch0 polled and produced ONE exception completion (the host's ARP request):
  RXDIAG ch=0 idx=0 len=60 status=37 err=1 port=11 vport=0 vlan=0
  desc=04000000 82e500c2 (32-byte descriptor captured)
  -> RXERR ACCEPTED (accepterr=1, vendor would drop) status=37 port=11 vport=0 len=60
  -> pie-trace RX port=11 len=60 status=37 (delivered to eth2's netdev)
- Host AF_PACKET sniff then saw the box's ARP REPLY on the wire:
  ARP src d4:0d:ab:xx:xx:xx -> dst 00:e0:4c:63:17:58 len 60.
  This is the first bidirectional frame exchange on our own OpenWrt/6.18 stack: wire -> PIE RX ->
  CPU (exception accepted) -> kernel ARP reply -> PIE TX -> wire.
- The host then sent its ICMP echo requests (sniff saw 6x IPv4 host->box len 98), but the box
  produced ZERO further RX completions and ping still shows 100% loss. So unicast frames to the
  box's MAC are not being punted/forwarded to the CPU - exactly the missing CFE L2/VLAN/CPU-port
  forwarding state (the vendor modules cannot load on 6.18). Broadcast/exception frames reach the
  CPU; normal unicast does not.
So the complete hardware path is proven for punted frames (RX+TX+netdev), and the only remaining
piece is the switch's L2/VLAN/CPU-port state that would let normal host unicast frames reach the
CPU (and later be forwarded). Next: QM lane to decode hi_kcara/hi_swa L2/VLAN/CPU-port init and
deliver a gated W17 stage, or an experiment to force punt/copy-to-CPU of unicast frames.
Evidence 2026-11-20-first-traffic.log.

## 2026-11-20 19:15 - reboot from our working image falls back to stock slot A: boot-selector/env handling is not implemented in our 6.18 userspace (overlay persistence across reboot untestable until fixed)

After the working W20 image 39424b94 passed ping/SSH and the overlay was rw, we wrote a persistence
marker (/root/persist-test) and rebooted from our own image (/sbin/reboot -f). The box came back
on the VENDOR 5.10 stack: the UART log shows the vendor modules (swa_netdevice_event, vap
interfaces) and stock is reachable at 192.168.10.1. So the reboot from our image selected slot A
(vendor) instead of returning to our slot B.
Implication: our own userspace does not maintain the bootloader selector/env that the vendor
userspace writes (sysenv boot_reg cell / ubi env), and the loader's failover logic chose the
vendor slot. The working image itself is fine; this is a boot-handover gap (the same class of
state the install path handles from stock via sysenv boot_reg=0x11). Overlay persistence across
reboot remains untestable until our userspace keeps the selector across reboot.
No physical recovery was needed: stock came up and is reachable, so we can reinstall the next
image from stock. Next: rebuild the canonical 001-058 image (canonical attended cmdline +
heartbeat) and reinstall from stock; then continue the verification matrix with the reboot item
marked blocked on boot-selector support, and add that support as a follow-up task.
Evidence 2026-11-20-reboot-fallback.log.

Patch 060 handoff probe result on hardware (image 202832a2, cmdline luofu_smp_handoff_probe=1):
  [0.000000] luofu-smp: handoff A=00000000 B=66cc66cc pen=80600080 scu_cfg=00000511
  [0.000000] luofu-smp: handoff verdict decompressor-entry=no kernel-stext=CONSUMED
  [0.000000] luofu-smp: handoff cpu1-ran monitor scu_cfg bit5=clear
  [0.353868] luofu-smp: handoff markers at prep A=00000000 B=66cc66cc
  [0.360252] luofu-smp: handoff cpu1-ran monitor at prep scu_cfg=00000511 bit5=clear
  [0.580545] luofu-smp: handoff cpu1-ran monitor post-release scu_cfg=00000511 bit5=clear
Interpretation: the decompressor-entry stub A was NOT consumed (CPU1 not polling yet at that instant),
but the kernel-stext stub B WAS consumed (marker nonzero, 0x66cc66cc) - CPU1 becomes active during the
decompressor window and executes our head.S stub. So CPU1 is alive and responsive; our normal
release path misses it (it probably starts polling after our early release attempt, and the pen is
then stale/already overwritten; later add_cpu(1) attempts found it spinning/consumed elsewhere).

jump when it changes - so platsmp/__cpu_up can later point the pen at the real secondary_startup
(with secondary_data set up) and CPU1 enters the normal SMP path. That would explain and likely fix
the 1-CPU limitation.

- /proc/device-tree/cpus/enable-method = "hisilicon,hsan_smp" (vendor string); cpu@0/cpu@1 nodes.

  (CPU0/CPU1 core gate/reset indices), resume-offset = 0x38, set-wdg-offset 0x50, clr-wdg 0x70,
  reboot-offset 0, reboot-base-index 0.
- reserved-memory/flashinfo node: reg = 0x80600000 size 0x4000, atag-offset = 0x1000 (ATAG at
  0x80601000), compatible "hsan,flashinfo_reserved" - the probe markers live in the first bytes of
  this window (0x80600010/0x80600020/0x80600040/0x80600080), which the vendor loader reserves.
- /proc/mtd: kernel slots kernela/kernelb = 0x00840000 = 8,650,752 bytes - the loader's image read
  bound is the slot size, so an uncompressed Image (~12 MiB) will NOT fit without a reduced config.
- Risky loader reads: 0x80040000 = 0x00000000, 0x800405e0 = 0xE2066007 (not the e5967000
  signature); top-2MiB signature scan found nothing (dd /dev/mem reads returned no data on stock;
  use devmem for windows there).
- GICD ITARGETSR8 (0x10181820) = 0x01010101 (IRQ32-35 target CPU0), so the enabled IRQ32/34 are not
  a CPU1 wakeup path.

protocol to prove the handoff), then boot and check 2 CPUs.

## 2026-11-20 22:20 - SMP SOLVED: 2 CPUs online and persistent. Root cause was the U-Boot handoff staging being aborted by missing DT nodes (console alias + flashinfo reserved-memory), not the kernel release path.

After the sentinel probe proved CPU1 never enters the kernel stubs even though U-Boot's in-place CPU1
poll loop (0x80040000, e5967000/0afffffc) is intact in RAM on our image, the load moved to the loader
side. The U-Boot boot path is bootcmd="mtd read kernel${bootflag} 0x83200000; bootfip 0x83200000"
(loadaddr 0x83200000); the custom bootfip does the pre-kernel handoff staging and prints, on stock:
  alias console=/uart1@0x1010f000
  serialnr->high=0x8250, serialnr->low=0x1010f000, atag_addr=0x80601000
Our boot printed "alias console not found" and skipped the serialnr/atag line.
DT fix: our DTS lacked the vendor base DTB's aliases/console property and the
reserved-memory/flashinfo node (compatible hsan,flashinfo_reserved, reg 0x80600000+0x4000,
atag-offset 0x1000). Added both (skeleton DTS + build clone).
Image d61c09e6 booted:
  alias console=/serial@1010f000
  serialnr->high=0x8250, serialnr->low=0x1010f000, atag_addr=0x80601000
  luofu-smp: handoff post-release cpu1-ran monitor scu_cfg=00000531 bit5=set
  smp: Brought up 1 node, 2 CPUs
  SMP: Total of 2 processors activated (3974.75 BogoMIPS)
  CPU1: thread -1, cpu 1, socket 0, mpidr 80000001
  /proc/cpuinfo = 2; online = 0-1; /proc/interrupts has CPU0/CPU1 columns (TWD active on both)
Reboot persistence: rebooted with the pair recorder active -> came back on rootfsb (pair b recorded),
2 CPUs again (Brought up 2 CPUs, 3987.86 BogoMIPS), ping 20/20 0% loss, SSH fine.
CONCLUSION: the kernel-side SMP release path (pen=secondary_startup + CRG resume + wakeup IPI) was
correct all along; the blocker was that the stock U-Boot bootfip handoff staging was aborted because
our DTB lacked the loader's expected console alias and flashinfo reserved-memory node, so CPU1 was
never set up to poll the pen. Adding those two DT items fixed SMP completely (060/061 probes remain
useful diagnostics; with the fix CPU1 consumes the real secondary_startup, so the sentinels stay
untouched exactly as observed).
Evidence 2026-11-20-smp-2cpu.log, smp-reboot capture, stock U-Boot preamble comparisons.

## 2026-11-21 11:45 - RETRACTION: the "2-CPU hang" was a host bench-link outage, not a kernel hang. The canonical 2-CPU image is stable and verified (soak in progress).

Overnight the bench host lost the USB-Ethernet link state: enp195s0f3u1 came up without carrier/IPs
(NetworkManager state changed), so both 192.168.1.1 and 192.168.10.1 pings failed and the UART
capture (timeout 1200 s) had already ended - the box looked dead. After the user power-cycled it, the
box booted its existing image and UART showed the 6.18 kernel + heartbeat still running (HB 297+),
and the host carrier returned once tools/bench-link.sh --apply restored the addresses. There is NO
evidence of a kernel hang: no Oops/panic/BUG/WARNING in the boot log (the only grep hit is the
literal "panic=0" in the cmdline), heartbeats continuous, and the box had been running normally.
Corrected status: the 2-CPU bring-up is stable; the maxcpus=1/lockdep images built for the false
hang remain available as diagnostics but are not needed for a stability bug.
Canonical image 974e6ca6 (patches 001-061 + DTS handoff fix + canonical cmdline + DEVMEM/devmem/pair
recorder) was installed from stock and verified:
- /proc/cpuinfo = 2, online 0-1, smp: Brought up 2 CPUs, Total of 2 processors (4000.97 BogoMIPS),
  CPU1 mpidr 80000001;
- br-lan 192.168.1.1/24 up, ping 20/20 0% loss, SSH fine, /overlay ubifs rw;
- boot log clean (no Oops/panic/BUG/WARNING).
A 15-minute continuous-ping soak is running to confirm; bench-link stability must be watched
overnight (add a carrier/IP check to the session start practice).
Lesson: "box unreachable" must be split into box-side and host-side checks before declaring a hang;
use bench-link.sh first, and only then UART/heartbeat evidence. The userspace heartbeat remains the
reliable liveness probe when the console log is available.

  RAs, i.e. the port is a LAN port in br-lan (eth0/eth1/eth2), not WAN. Box->host egress works on
  any port, but host->box ingress needs CPU delivery, and the W17/W19 CPU-copy mirror workaround
  is programmed only for eth2 (switch port 11, dst 4).

  GEMAC switch ports (9/10/11/12 per the vendor port map): mirror each source port to the CPU
  destination AND deliver the RX completion to the matching netdev (current cpucopy_port=11
  hardcodes eth2). That is the next net-driver task; native CFE-equivalent forwarding remains the
  separate long-term track. Until then the bench LAN port is the previously working eth2 port.

## 2026-11-21 16:20 - Multi-port source-port experiment RESULT: no source identifier in CPU-copy completions -> native L2/VLAN bridge is required for multi-port LAN/WAN.

- Setup: probe image a91ebcf0 (mirror_src_mask=0x1e00 covering ports 9-12, rxdiag=1) installed on
  the unit via the verified telnet installer (selector 0x11, active stock pair unchanged). Cable
  was moved to the far-right LAN jack, host ping loop ran, router was power-cycled so the probe
  image booted with only that jack connected. The UART capture missed the boot window, but the
  fresh-boot dmesg retained the 24 capped RXDIAG lines (boot_id
  45df3d10-72ad-43a4-bc2a-88df40710639), which is what the analysis uses.
- Evidence: build/evidence-bench-gates/multi-port-probe/{eth2-baseline-rxdiag.txt,
  far-right-jack-rxdiag.txt}. The unique field tuples (ch,len,status,err,port,vport,vlan) are
  IDENTICAL for both jacks: (1,74,0,0,0,0,0), (1,66,0,0,0,0,0), (1,88,0,0,0,0,0),
  (0,60,0,0,0,0,0), (0,60,37,1,11,0,0). Descriptor words: only word0=0x04000000 and word1=DMA|0xc2
  are nonzero; words 2..7 are zero for every mirrored completion. No source-port/vport field.
- Conclusions: (1) the extended mirror mask does mirror the other jacks to CPU dst 4; (2) the
  CPU-copy completion cannot identify the source jack, so per-port delivery is impossible with
  this workaround; (3) multi-port LAN/WAN requires the native L2/VLAN hardware bridge
  (LSW-SPEC, separate project). Do not ship a mirror-mask multi-port hack.
- Recorded in opensource/docs/MULTI-PORT-PLAN.md (measured result + decision) and RELEASE-NOTES.
  The board was switched back to stock and the known-good image 7421bb7a reinstalled afterwards;
  probe artifacts (patch 066, image a91ebcf0) remain bench-only.
- Also during this round: submission package verified (MANIFEST 102/102) and parent bumped to
  fa76c97 (submodule c931c74); curated-sync lane re-dispatched with /home-based workdirs.

## 2026-11-21 16:55 - Watchdog telemetry/arming verified indirectly: /dev/watchdog is already held open (Resource busy) with state=active/timeout=30, so the hardware watchdog is armed and serviced by userspace (procd), and the box stays up across minutes -> keepalive path works.

- Runtime: /sys/class/watchdog/watchdog0/{state,timeout,identity,nowayout} = active / 30 s /
  "HiSilicon luofu watchdog" / 0. Writing the sysfs timeout returns EACCES (the current driver
  exposes start/stop/ping but no set_timeout sysfs store), and opening /dev/watchdog returns
  EBUSY: userspace (procd watchdog) already owns the device and services it. The box has been
  continuously up for minutes with the device busy, which is exactly the keepalive path.
- A forced-fire test would require stopping the PID-1 watchdog service (or rmmod/reboot games),
  which risks the box for no additional evidence; the armed/serviceable state plus long stable
  uptimes is recorded as [V]/[I] instead.
- This also explains the earlier cleaned-DTS boot failure: that kernel never reached userspace
  (stalled in MTD registration), so procd never opened /dev/watchdog and the U-Boot 30 s

  nonstandard/reserved encoding, but GIC-400 PPI configuration is read-only/fixed by the SoC
  integration, so the DT flag cannot change the hardware.

  IRQ_TYPE_LEVEL_HIGH; recommendation to the upstream lane: document the measured read-only value,
  draft the DTS as GIC_PPI 13 | CPU mask | IRQ_TYPE_LEVEL_HIGH (standard convention), and treat
  the flag flip as a separate ACTIVE DTS delta that must be hardware-boot-tested before adoption
  (it cannot break the fixed PPI config, but our rule is boot-test every active change).

## 2026-11-21 18:55 - Recovery succeeded but the subsequent handover left a MIXED kernel/userland system: our 6.18 kernel (cmdline luofu_switch.*) booted with the stock 5.10 rootfs (rootfsb). Stock LuCI then refuses the wizard ("Invalid board info!", bdinfo checkuuid needs the vendor kernel's /proc/sys/dev/flash_uuid) and the MQTT broker path is silent.

- Timeline: RESET-hold recovery restored stock (U-Boot RESET counter 2 s, RRQ recovery.bin from
  192.168.1.88, 20,975,775 B) and stock answered at 192.168.10.1. The telnet installer then ran and
  reported "stock selector cell 0x11 -> active pair b, write pair a": it wrote our flashinfo-test
  image kernel to /dev/mtd11 and rootfs to /dev/mtd13 and set selector 0x10. U-Boot on the next
  boot logged "bootflag b bootreg 10" and loaded the KERNEL from kernelb (an older 6.18 image;
  cmdline ubi.mtd=rootfsb ... luofu_switch.* luofu_pie.accepterr=1) while the ROOTFS attached was
  mtd14 "rootfsb" - the stock 5.10 squashfs. So the running system is 6.18 kernel + stock userland.
- Consequences: the stock web UI serves the first-run wizard but renders "Invalid board info!"
  because bdinfo checkuuid compares the signed bdinfo against /proc/sys/dev/flash_uuid, which only
  the vendor 5.10 kernel exposes; the wizard POST therefore 403s (tried single/double hash, page
  and constant salt, all variants). The MQTT broker accepts the forged JWT (CONNACK rc=0) but
  cmagent never answers (same missing board-info/kernel contract), so the CVE command chain is dead
  in this mixed state. Stock admin password is unset, so no authenticated route either.
- Lesson for the installer: after a recovery, the U-Boot env bootflag can override the slot the
  installer wrote; the installer must set/verify the env bootflag and the rootfs pair together, and
  verify the booted kernel cmdline/rootfs pair after reboot (not just ping+SSH+2 CPUs). This mixed
  state must never be presented as a successful install (the tool's PASS/FAIL did catch the SSH
  failure, but the handover itself was wrong).
- Next: one more RESET-hold recovery (physical) restores a consistent stock kernel+rootfs pair; then
  verify the broker channel with box-provision --cmd id BEFORE any flash, and only then install
  our image with both env bootflag and selector set consistently (or via the broker channel).

## 2026-11-22 17:05 - *** BREAKTHROUGH: PCIe LINK TRAINS ON THE 6.18 IMAGE. Root cause was NEVER the PCIe register program - it was BOARD GPIO state. *** Method: built a standalone loadable 6.18 module (luofu_standalone.ko) replicating the vendor hi_pcie.ko sequence with NO DWC framework; it first failed too (link LTSSM 0x00). Then bisected GPIO0 controller state: stock (vendor kernel) drives GPIO0 DDR=0x1330000f / DATA=0x12300004; our image drives DDR=0x0300000f / DATA=0x0300000f. Writing the STOCK values to 0x10106000/0x10106004 and re-running the standalone module: LTSSM=0x11 (L0), DEBUG0=0x03d15111, DEBUG1=0x08000110, and config read cfg[0]=0x000559e7 (the Wi-Fi endpoint answered). Bisect results: DATA bits 0/1/3/24 high are harmless; setting DATA to ours (clearing bits 25/28) DROPS the link; restoring recovers it automatically. DDR: pin21 as output is REQUIRED, pin28 as output is REQUIRED, pin20 output is not. Thus GPIO0 pin28 must be OUTPUT HIGH (PERST deassert / power) and pin21 OUTPUT LOW - the Wi-Fi endpoint's power/reset controls on this board. Our DTS has no node for 20/21/28 (stock kernel configures them). FIX applied in pcie-luofu driver host_init: ioremap 0x10106000, DDR |= BIT(21)|BIT(28), DATA = (DATA & ~BIT(21)) | BIT(28)  -> W25a build. Endpoint config space read live from working link: vendor 0x59e7 device 0x0005, class 0x02800000 (network controller), bars 4/4/4, rev 0xe5.

## 2026-11-22 17:20 - GPIO root cause pinned down EXACTLY (hardware-verified by runtime bisect on W25a/W25b): the Wi-Fi endpoint (Hi5622/TR5220) needs GPIO0 pins 20, 21 and 28 to be OUTPUTS driven HIGH before PCIe training. Stock (vendor kernel) GPIO0 state: DDR=0x1330000f, DATA=0x12300004 -> output pins 0,1,2,3,20,21,24,25,28 with 20,21,28 all high. Our image (DTS gpio-leds on 0,1,2,3,24,25, no node for 20/21/28) left 20/21/28 as inputs and drove 0,1,3,24 high (LEDs off, active-low). Bisect results: (a) DATA=0x1330000f + DDR=0x1330000f (LEDs-high plus 20/21/28 high) -> LTSSM=0x11 L0, cfg=0x000559e7; (b) DATA=0x12300004 + same DDR -> also trains; (c) any of bits 20/21/28 low (data or direction) -> no link. So fix = ddr |= BIT(20)|BIT(21)|BIT(28) and data |= BIT(20)|BIT(21)|BIT(28) in host_init (plus msleep(1000) settle because our probe is at ~2.5 s while the vendor module runs ~11 s). W25d is the image with this exact fix.
